item.text:
I found and reproduced a concrete defect this turn.

**F2 — the admin `snapshot` command's rate limit is 1000× looser than documented.** [Commands.java:766](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_01-10-40-zookeeper-baseline/work/zookeeper-server/src/main/java/org/apache/zookeeper/server/admin/Commands.java:766) builds the limiter as `new RateLimiter(1, rateLimiterInterval, TimeUnit.MICROSECONDS)`, while the sibling `RestoreCommand` at line 646 uses `TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS`. `rateLimiterInterval` is read from `zookeeper.admin.rateLimiterIntervalInMS` (default `300000`), and `zookeeperAdmin.md` documents that property as "The time interval for rate limiting admin command to protect the server. Defaults to 5 mins." `RateLimiter` converts via `unit.toMillis(...)`, so the snapshot endpoint effectively allows one request per **300 ms** instead of 5 minutes: an authenticated admin client can force whole-datatree snapshot streaming several times a second, defeating the documented protection. Conditions: admin endpoint enabled, `serializeLastProcessedZxid` enabled, `Perms.ALL` on `/`.

Reproduction (production objects, source tree untouched):

```
SnapshotCommand rate limiter intervalInMs = 300
RestoreCommand  rate limiter intervalInMs = 300000
same RateLimiter parameter as RestoreCommand? false
documented (5 min) interval honoured by snapshot? false
snapshot limiter: first=true secondImmediately=false secondAfter400ms=true
```

Helper kept separately at [work/repro/SnapshotRateLimitCheck.java](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_01-10-40-zookeeper-baseline/work/repro/SnapshotRateLimitCheck.java) with the compile/run command and output in `repro/out.txt`; details and the checked alternative explanations ("maybe the 300 ms limit is intentional") are in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_01-10-40-zookeeper-baseline/work/report.md) §3 as F2. Honest caveat recorded there too: without a reference tree I cannot say whether this unit bug is injected or pre-existing upstream; what is established is that the shipped code contradicts its own documented default and its sibling command.

This explains why the test sweep missed it — the `server/admin` test classes (`CommandsTest`, `SnapshotAndRestoreCommandTest`) were among the few never executed, and none of the exercised tests assert the interval.

Remaining leads if the audit continues (report §6): run `server/admin` tests and, if useful, an end-to-end `/commands/snapshot` check that two rapid POSTs return 200/200 instead of 200/429; plus the earlier list (unrunnable `QuorumSSLTest`/Kerberos/hammer classes, the two hostname-blocked FLE election tests, and the rest of the 3.9.x fix checklist).
